Mkun (CHE203): Sir is a very kind faculty who explains all topics clearly. He writes out the structures of amino acids, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids during lectures which makes memorisation much easier. The only issue is that his handwriting is not always easy to understand. He takes 4 quizzes and counts the best 3. The quizzes include MCQs and structure-based questions and he also gives assignments focused only on structures. He takes one midterm, which includes MCQs, short “explain why” questions and structures. The final exam follows the same pattern. He curves a lot, his marking is lenient, and he gives partial marks. If you do proper self-study, go through his slides thoroughly and take notes on whatever he emphasises during lectures (such as which structures or mechanisms are important), it becomes much easier to secure an A/A– in this course. And please don’t be late to class—he will literally scream at you if you arrive even 1 minute late.
Overall rating: 9/10

mar5.review: Che203- MAR5- In simple words, just brilliant. Every time I attended his class I felt so motivated and felt like knowing and learning as much as one can. The course itself is quite hard. It’s full of long ass mechanisms, structures, and other complex chemistries and even the theoretical questions are conceptual. If you take this course under him, remember two things. One, time management can be a huge issue in quizzes, so be prepared for that mentally. Two, be attentive in his class, not everything he mentions during lectures is on the slides. Take notes or photos as necessary. Counts 3/4 quiz. Other assessments are mid and final. Questions in mid or final are relatively straight forward. He doesn’t curve though and gives you exactly what you deserve.

regardless of what most people say that his questions are very difficult, timing is not adequate blah blah..that's mostly bs. Sir is responsive to emails and is available in his office hours. Good luck.
